Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has dismissed allegations that he installed Governor Usman Ododo as a political stooge. Bello insisted that his successor was selected on merit and has demonstrated his ability to govern independently. He said Ododo was chosen from among several contenders because he was considered the most qualified person to lead the state at the time, adding that the governor had continued to justify the confidence placed in him. The former governor stated this in an interview with Channels Television on Friday. He argued that political opponents were free to make allegations during election seasons but maintained that Ododo was now demonstrating his leadership capacity. “During political seasons, anybody is free to say whatever they want. Without going too far, today, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, who has been called so many unprintable names, is proving that he is Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, taking the lead from the front,” Bello said. Explaining how the decision to support Ododo was reached, Bello said he refused to allow ethnic, religious or regional considerations to influence the choice of the party’s candidate. According to him, several options were available, but Ododo stood out as the most suitable person for the position. “You see, at that time, there were so many options available for us and the people of Kogi State, especially from our party first. But as the leader of the party and the state, at that time, I refused to allow sentiments of tribe, of religion, or where you come from, to influence my decision or our decision,” he said. He added that the decision was collectively taken within their political circle after considering the qualifications of the aspirants. “So collectively, as a member of a political family, we now decided that, look, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, though from the same Kogi Central, is more qualified. And then, by the grace of God, the people of Kogi overwhelmingly voted him into office, and he’s doing excellently well now,” Bello said. Asked whether he still considered Ododo the right person to lead Kogi, Bello maintained that his assessment had not changed. “As at the time we chose him, he’s the best, and today, he is still the best to lead the state to the promised land,” he said. Bello also expressed confidence that Ododo would secure a second term, predicting that voters would reward the governor for his performance. Rejecting the suggestion that he had imposed Ododo on the people, the former governor insisted that the electorate made the final decision through the ballot. “The people elected him, and 101%, I am very, very sure and very, very confident that the people will re-elect him again, when the time comes for his second term, because of his performance,” he said. He further argued that Ododo’s record in public service, both as Auditor-General for Local Government and as governor, had strengthened his standing among residents. “Even when he was in office then, as the Auditor General for local government, and now as the Executive Governor, his performance in less than three years has really sold him out to the people,” Bello added. 2027: Group drums up support for Tinubu, Ododo in Kogi INEC begins distribution of 86,931 PVCs in Kogi I’m not bargaining for Rivers gov ticket – Tonye Cole On his own eight-year tenure as governor, Bello said he had no regrets about his administration, although he was still reviewing his record in office. Asked to identify his biggest regret, he responded, “Well, I have no regret whatsoever. I have no regret whatsoever. I take responsibility for everything that happened.” He said he inherited a state that required firm leadership and believed his administration had provided the direction needed to move it forward. “I met a state that was in need of leadership. Decisive leadership. And I provided it at that time,” he said. Bello also insisted that he gave his best during his time in office, while acknowledging that the expectations of the people of Kogi remained high. “Well, my people are so interesting that our best may never be enough, because we strive to always be ahead of others, especially knowing where we’re coming from,” he said. He added that the circumstances confronting his administration were difficult, citing economic, political, social, and other challenges. “If anything, considering the prevailing economic, political, physical, social, even spiritual situation at that time, we gave our best,” Bello said. He maintained that his administration, which he described as the New Direction Administration, had rescued the state and placed it on a development path. “We were able to rescue the state and put it on the path of proper development. We turned our administration then as New Direction Administration,” he said. Bello also expressed satisfaction that Ododo, whom he described as one of his mentees, had continued from where his administration stopped. “We provided that leadership, and thank God, from amongst, let’s say, my mentees, the current governor, is now leading the state from where we stopped in the right direction,” he said. Ododo emerged as the All Progressives Congress candidate for the November 11, 2023 Kogi governorship election after serving as the state’s Auditor-General for Local Governments under Yahaya Bello. His emergence as the party’s candidate attracted attention because he was widely regarded as Bello’s preferred successor. Ododo went on to win the election with 446,237 votes, defeating his closest challenger, Murtala Ajaka of the Social Democratic Party, who polled 259,052 votes. He was sworn in on January 27, 2024, succeeding Bello, who had completed two terms in office. The relationship between the two politicians has remained a subject of public and political discussion, with critics questioning the extent of Bello’s influence over the incumbent governor. In February 2026, for instance, a pressure group accused Ododo of being a puppet in his predecessor’s political affairs, an allegation that forms part of the wider debate over the governor’s independence.
